headline.title: The UK Will Scan Asylum-Seekers’ Faces for Age Checks—Despite Knowing the Tech Is Flawed
headline.summary: The UK Home Office plans to implement facial recognition technology to verify the ages of asylum seekers, despite internal tests revealing significant risks of inaccuracies. Critics have raised concerns about the potential for life-altering errors associated with the flawed technology.

articles.title: Midjourney goes from generating cat images to full-body ultrasound scans
articles.summary: Midjourney has unveiled its first hardware product, The Midjourney Scanner, an ultrasound-based full-body scanner designed to capture detailed images using a ring of sensors. CEO David Holz also announced plans to establish a spa in San Francisco, marking a significant shift from the company's initial focus on AI-generated images.

articles.title: France Advances Europe’s AI Future With NVIDIA Technologies
articles.summary: France is implementing its AI strategy by leveraging NVIDIA technologies, with new AI factories and enhanced national compute capacity now operational. The initiative has led to the deployment of AI agents in production and the emergence of startups within the French AI ecosystem.

articles.title: Tesco moving 40,000 server workloads off VMware amid Broadcom's “abusive conduct”
articles.summary: Tesco is transferring 40,000 server workloads away from VMware, citing a 175 percent price increase imposed by Broadcom as a key factor. The decision follows legal filings in the UK where Tesco accused Broadcom of "abusive conduct" in its pricing practices.

articles.title: Nothing from Something: Can a Language Model Discover 0?
articles.summary: A recent study explores the potential of AI systems, particularly those based on artificial neural networks, to extend human mathematical knowledge by discovering new mathematical concepts beyond their training data. The research emphasizes the importance of out-of-distribution generalization in enabling these systems to hypothesize novel mathematical structures.

articles.title: Towards Distributed Inference of LLMs on a P2P Network
articles.summary: The article presents a decentralized routing scheme for peer-to-peer serving of large language models (LLMs), aimed at reducing inference latency through prefix caching. It details a method where each node maintains a local radix tree of cached prefixes and periodically updates estimates of peer caches to enhance efficiency in a distributed environment.

articles.title: Agentic Discovery of Non-Canonical Antimicrobial Peptides with AMPGAN v3
articles.summary: Researchers have developed AMPGAN v3, a multi-objective conditional GAN designed to generate antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that include non-natural amino acids and chemical modifications, addressing the limitations of current generative models. This advancement aims to enhance the design of AMPs as potential solutions to combat antimicrobial resistance, which contributes to over a million deaths annually.

articles.title: MLLP-VRAIN UPV system for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task
articles.summary: The MLLP-VRAIN research group presented their approach for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task, employing the Parakeet and Qwen 3.5 models to develop a robust cascaded solution. Their work focuses on adaptive "black-box" policies and explores relaxations to improve quality-latency trade-offs in long-form SimulST.

articles.title: SegTME-UNI2: A Foundation Model-Based Framework for Generalisable Multiclass Cell Segmentation and LLM-Driven Tumour Microenvironment Characterisation in Histopathology
articles.summary: The SEGTME-UNI2 framework integrates a dual-head segmentation model to enhance multiclass cell segmentation and tumour microenvironment characterization from H&E-stained histology images. Built on the UNI2-H pathology foundation model, it aims to improve feature extraction and clinical reporting in histopathology.

articles.title: ED3R: Energy-Aware Distributed Disaster Detection Enabled by Cooperative Robotic Agents
articles.summary: The paper presents ED3R, an energy-aware distributed framework designed for cooperative robotic agents to enhance disaster detection and environmental monitoring. It addresses the challenges of making decisions under uncertainty and resource constraints during critical missions, such as wildfires, by optimizing energy usage and detection time.

articles.title: Human-in-the-Loop Atlas-Based 3D Asset Segmentation for Interactive Content Workflows
articles.summary: The article presents a human-in-the-loop pipeline designed for segmenting 3D assets into meaningful regions, addressing the challenges posed by application-dependent criteria that require user control. This method generates a segmented 2D parameterized atlas from a 3D model, facilitating workflows in interactive media, gaming, and XR content.

articles.title: High-Fidelity 3D Geometric Reconstruction of Pelvic Organs from MRI: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Iterative Optimization Approach
articles.summary: A new study presents a hybrid deep learning and iterative optimization approach for high-fidelity 3D geometric reconstruction of pelvic organs from MRI, addressing the challenges of labor-intensive and poorly standardized methods. This framework aims to enhance patient-specific pelvic floor modeling and analysis by improving the quality of reconstructed geometries.
